definition: An unsupervised learning technique that groups data points into clusters based on similarity, without predefined labels.
details: Common clustering algorithms include k-means and hierarchical clustering, used for tasks like customer segmentation, anomaly detection, and exploratory data analysis.
story: Picture a librarian organizing a million slips of paper so that any one of them can be found in a heartbeat. Think of it this way: An unsupervised learning technique that groups data points into clusters based on similarity, without predefined labels. And here is the clever part: Common clustering algorithms include k-means and hierarchical clustering, used for tasks like customer segmentation, anomaly detection, and exploratory data analysis. Garbage in, garbage out — and the reverse: clean, representative data makes the model quietly brilliant. And that is Clustering — the unglamorous work everything else stands on.
